commands.text: The chapel doors stand open. Candlelight pours across the square, and names have been tied to the eaves on narrow cards.
At dusk, St. Maria closes its shops. Bakers, guards, children and scavengers gather without being called.
The first bell names the living. When Agnes speaks your name, the village answers: RETURNED.
At midnight, lanterns are carried to the Labyrinth gate. The second bell names those who remain below.
After the final name, something beneath St. Maria rings a third time.
Every flame bends toward the gate. One extinguished lantern relights by itself.
Nobody moves until the sound stops. Then everyone moves at once, and very quickly, as though the square had been cleared by weather.

commands.text: "Two bells are ours. We ring them. The third is not ours and we do not ring it."

Every few years, a Summoner
comes to St. Maria.
You did not come alone.

Saban carried you through the rain.
He was your mount—and your only summon.

St. Maria noticed him
before it noticed you.

The village made room.
Barely.

One bed. One bowl.
Five empty rooms.

Below the town, every bond
is recorded as a debt.

Beyond the gate, souls lose
their edges.

You came for impossible things.
The first was already beside you.

ST. MARIA
Late Autumn

PASSAGE HOUSE — ROOM 3

"This'll be home for both of you." The key is still turning in the lock outside when the footsteps begin to recede.
The other Summoner rooms are empty. Yours has been cleaned, but not emptied of its previous lives. Someone has dragged a feed bowl in from the stable.
Saban noses the bowl, then leans his familiar weight against you. He carried you to St. Maria; now your mount and only summon will carry you below it.

45.name: Return Beat - The Half-Contract Comes Up

commands.text:
PASSAGE HOUSE -- ROOM 3

You did not come here first. You came here anyway; your feet did it while you were thinking about the paper.
The Half-Contract has dried on the walk up. It is a creature's half. Four signatures, one owner, and the owner's side torn away and gone.
You have seen the hand before, backward, in blue chalk on a wall that was warm.
Someone has been in the room. The bed is made the way you do not make it. The feed bowl has been moved to where a larger animal could reach it.
Nothing. Nothing at all is missing. Something has been added: a second bowl, smaller, dry, and never used.

options.label: Leave it exactly as you found it.

commands.text: You close the door and stand in the corridor for a while, listening to five empty rooms.
Outside, St. Maria is doing the thing towns do after a Vigil: working loudly, so that nobody has to be quiet.
Take the paper to Agnes, and the stairs down after. The way you went down, she said.
The bell has no clapper and never has. It has been ringing for eleven years with nothing inside it.
The Warden's iron tongue is warm in your hand. It fits. Of course it fits.
Above you, through nine hundred feet of rock, St. Maria is asleep and countable.
A name goes in with the clapper. That is the whole of the mechanism. Whoever is named is what the bell means.
You say it once, quietly, the way the Registrar taught you to say it at the gate.
The bell takes it. The sound goes up and does not come back down.

You are still in the ledger.
You are simply no longer at the top of it.

St. Maria rang two bells that winter
and did not discuss the third.

You came for impossible things.
You were charged for one.

ST. MARIA -- EARLY WINTER

The walk up took two days and you do not remember either of them.
Nine days later a woman you have never met stops you in the square and says your name correctly, and cries, and cannot explain why.
Agnes rings two bells at the next Vigil. The third answers in your voice, and the village -- which has agreed not to ask -- says RETURNED.
You did not get rich. You got remembered, which in St. Maria is the more expensive of the two.
The clean bell in the Rusted Choir knew your name before you gave it away. You have decided not to think about the order of those two events.
You still have the small change from the Rusted Choir. St. Maria mint. It spends.
One thin ordinary note from a rusted bell, and you walked out on the other four. You are almost sure that was the right number.
You crossed the Rusted Choir with your hands at your sides and it has bothered you ever since, which was presumably the arrangement.
The Vault still has your name on its counterweight. You got a seed and a leaf for it. Nobody has mispronounced you yet.
Three hundred coins, and the Weighing Room was appalled. You would do it again. That is the appalling part.
NOT YOURS TO WEIGH. YOU ARE HOLDING IT FOR SOMEONE. You have stopped arguing with the chalk.
In the Garden Without Wind your leaf hung at the height of your face and told you the terms. You cannot say you were not told the terms.
There is a second feed bowl in Room 3, smaller, still dry. You have not moved it and you do not intend to.
Cerberus cost six MP a step for the whole campaign and was worth exactly none of it, and you would not give him back.
